verdict.rationale: Keycloak's own docs cover headless, scripted operation. It runs in a container with the admin user bootstrapped from environment variables, and it ships the kcadm.sh Admin CLI and an Admin REST API. Realms can be imported and exported as JSON, the operator handles declarative client and realm-import automation, health endpoints support CI readiness checks, and client-credentials service accounts allow machine access. Hands-on reports say the admin API is inconsistent, which makes idempotent Ansible automation hard. They also say config held in the database is hard to keep in sync or promote as code, leaning on the third-party keycloak-config-cli. missing for 10: consistent idempotent admin API behavior, first-party declarative config-as-code sync outside the operator, CI-specific documentation such as a test-container guide.
